title: Production Manager Memo: Credit Schedule on Escalated Orders — Factory Production Orders
content:
**Memo.** For Factory Production Orders, the escalation schedule of the on-time guarantee follows the delay notices on the order, of every cause, compared with the class escalation count of **3** delay notices (the same in every build class):

| Delay notices on the order | How the credited weeks are paid |
|---|---|
| more than 3 | the first **2** credited weeks at the weekly credit rate, and every credited week beyond 2 at **1.5 times** that rate |
| exactly 3 | **one** more credited week is added, and every credited week is paid at the weekly credit rate |
| fewer than 3 | every credited week at the weekly credit rate |

The credited weeks are the weeks the credit is figured on, counted only when at least one full week late results. The weekly credit rate, times the units on the order, times the credited weeks as this schedule pays them, gives the amount of the credit before the class cap per order.

## Records read

All delay notices on the order's milestone records, whatever their cause — glass supplier, factory capacity, weather and freight, customer hold, late acknowledgment and customer specification remake alike.

## Weeks' worth paid (hypothetical credited weeks)

| Credited weeks | More than 3 notices | Exactly 3 notices | 2 notices |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 2 | 3 | 2 |
| 4 | 2 and 3, 5 | 5 | 4 |
| 6 | 2 and 6, 8 | 7 | 6 |

## Hypothetical example

An order with 5 delay notices, 4 credited weeks, 3 units and a weekly credit rate of 30.00: 5 weeks' worth at 30.00 for each of 3 units is 450.00 before the class cap.
